answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce deposit before earning rewards, then slash it when audits find identities controlled by the same actor claiming multiple shares. Auditors compare signed task histories and control patterns, so changing names does not erase evidence. A public cipher can verify records, while violet flags mark suspicious clusters for review. The attacker must tie up real capital for every identity and risks losing each bond; scaling a fake swarm raises both costs and exposure with the tide.
